articles.title: Dynasties stronger in poverty-stricken areas – CEAP
articles.summary: Strong dynastic presence is linked to some areas with poverty, inequality, weaker human development outcomes and political violence, according to the Catholic Educational Association of the…

blocks.text: October 6, 2026 | 12:00am

Citing a study, the CEAP said effects vary across provinces and regions, “but the institutional concern remains clear: democracy suffers when political power becomes difficult for ordinary citizens to enter and difficult for institutions to challenge.”
STAR / File

MANILA, Philippines — Strong dynastic presence is linked to some areas with poverty, inequality, weaker human development outcomes and political violence, according to the Catholic Educational Association of the Philippines.
Last month, the Supreme Court ruled that Congress has a mandatory constitutional duty to enact an anti-political dynasty law and the prolonged inaction had exceeded a reasonable period.

“A second-degree limit covers immediate family relationships. A fourth-degree limit reaches a wider network of blood and marital relationships and addresses the possibility of political families distributing positions among relatives beyond the immediate household,” the CEAP said.

Concentrating political power in the hands of a few families “weakens political competition and narrows access to public service. It can deepen patronage, clientelism, vote-buying and political dependency,” the group stressed.
Ecological protection belongs in the political dynasty debate, the CEAP said.

“The issue concerns who controls decisions over resources that affect everyone. It concerns who receives the benefits and who carries the costs. It concerns environmental justice, human dignity, participation and the protection of creation for present and future generations,” the CEAP said.

articles.title: Marcos orders government to prepare for widespread drought
articles.summary: President Marcos has ordered government agencies to prepare for the worst-case scenario as nearly all provinces in the country are expected to experience drought or very dry conditions due to the…

blocks.text: October 6, 2026 | 12:00am
A farmer in Barangay Central, San Jose, Occidental Mindoro checks the dry soil during El Niño in this file photo from March 2024.
Edd Gumban

MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos has ordered government agencies to prepare for the worst-case scenario as nearly all provinces in the country are expected to experience drought or very dry conditions due to the looming “super El Niño.”

Marcos issued the directive yesterday during a meeting with the heads of various agencies, including the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), Department of Agriculture, Department of Science and Technology and its attached agency, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration.

According to Science Secretary Renato Solidum, all provinces could experience drought or very dry conditions by the end of March 2027, although the severity would vary depending on the amount of rainfall received in different areas.
Some provinces, he noted, may experience more pronounced dry conditions only in the coming months.
Environment Secretary Juan Miguel Cuna said the possible declaration of a climate emergency was not discussed during the meeting.

“Nothing specific like that was discussed earlier, but the directive is for us to prepare for the worst-case scenario. I think that was discussed extensively, ensuring that the various agencies and sectors are ready should that happen,” he said.
Cuna said the DENR would revive its water conservation campaign, stressing that everyone has a role in protecting the country’s water supply.

He added that the country could not continue with business as usual and called on the public to avoid unnecessary water use, including excessive water use for car washing, cleaning driveways and other nonessential activities.

As part of preparations for the expected dry spell, the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) is also fast-tracking the construction of infrastructure for stormwater harvesting to support flood mitigation and disaster resilience.

Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon said the agency is prioritizing underground water detention basins in areas with floodwater pumping stations, including perennially flooded areas such as Roxas Boulevard and España in Manila, as well as parts of Bulacan and Pampanga.

During an inspection of an underground water detention basin being built by the DPWH-National Capital Region, Dizon said the project would link dedicated piping and pump systems to store rainwater from the Roxas Boulevard drainage network and nearby pumping stations.
The harvested water would then be routed to supply Maria Orosa Park, Plaza Rajah Sulayman and the Manila Baywalk area.
Civil works for the Rajah Sulayman retention facility are expected to be completed by February next year.

“This serves as DPWH’s direct contribution to preparing for incoming super El Niño dry spells,” Dizon said. “While we manage severe rainfall during the wet season, we are simultaneously building storage capacity so that harvested rainwater can be repurposed to maintain public parks during months of severe drought.”

To ensure stormwater reaches the underground network efficiently, the DPWH has launched a regionwide initiative across all engineering districts in Metro Manila to enlarge road inlets and catch basins.
Inlet expansion projects are underway along major arterial corridors, including España, G. Araneta Avenue, Mother Ignacia Avenue, EDSA and South Superhighway.
Dizon, however, stressed that enlarged drainage networks would remain ineffective if clogged by solid waste.
He appealed to local residents and barangay leaders to practice proper waste disposal and keep surface inlets free of debris. — Rainier Allan Ronda

articles.title: IBC-13 launches Senate TV
articles.summary: The Intercontinental Broadcasting Corp.welcomed the launch of Senate TV, a high-definition channel dedicated to the work of the Senate, now available on IBC Digital TV Channel 13.3.

blocks.text: October 6, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — The Intercontinental Broadcasting Corp. (IBC-13) welcomed the launch of Senate TV, a high-definition channel dedicated to the work of the Senate, now available on IBC Digital TV Channel 13.3.
The channel is leased by the Senate from IBC-13, which owns and operates the frequency.

Senate TV joins Congress TV (Channel 13.2), which IBC-13 launched in October 2024. Together, the two channels lay the groundwork for a C-SPAN-style framework for the Philippines: a public affairs service that shows viewers how their government works, with as little editorial filtering as possible.

In its first phase, Senate TV will air hearings and other proceedings of the chamber, following the path Congress TV took at its own launch. The channel will carry the Senate’s work as it happens, without commentary meant to steer how viewers should read it.
The programming is also meant to go beyond the session hall. Senate TV will follow members out of their chambers and into the communities they serve, down to the everyday Filipino.
A second phase is planned, as it was for Congress TV: Senate TV’s own main newscast wrapping up the activities of the Senate and its members, along with niche programs of its own.
C-SPAN, founded in the US in 1979 by Brian Lamb, and the cable industry, is widely regarded as a benchmark for impartial coverage of government.
It points its cameras at congressional sessions, hearings and public affairs events, and it does not employ reporters to interpret them.
Independent media watchdogs such as AllSides and Media Bias/Fact Check rate it as Center or Least Biased, and its audience includes a mix of conservatives, liberals and moderates.

On the launch, IBC-13 president and CEO Jose “Jimmie” Policarpio Jr. said Senate TV joins Congress TV under the franchise of IBC-13, which commits the whole organization to the delivery of accurate and timely information relevant to the needs of the Filipino people.

“Although IBC-13 is part of the integrated state media, we remain wholly committed to non-partisan coverage of events, for the welfare of the nation. We welcome Senate TV in fulfilling this mandate,” he said.

For the Senate, a dedicated channel gives the chamber a permanent, accessible record of its work. Debates, committee hearings and legislative deliberations reach the public in full, rather than only as clips and soundbites that often survive a news cycle.

The launch comes after two years of rebuilding at IBC-13. In 2024, the network settled more than half a billion pesos in retirement obligations that had weighed on it for over two decades, and initiated a corporate reorganization.
In 2025, more than P1.1 billion was mobilized to fund unpaid benefits for 388 employees, complete the reorganization and support the shift to digital.
Senate TV is available on IBC Digital TV Channel 13.3 in areas served by IBC-13’s digital broadcast. Viewers with digital TV sets or set-top boxes may need to rescan channels to find it.
Channel 13.3 had been carrying the dwAN 1206 AM simulcast.
Senate TV will use the channel until IBC-13 activates its fourth digital TV channel, which will then become the home of dwAN, ang Radyo ng Bagong Pilipinas.

articles.title: 49 minors rounded up for cyber threats – PNP
articles.summary: Forty-nine minors have been rounded up in the past months for instigating cyber threats that disrupted school classes.

blocks.text: October 6, 2026 | 12:00am
Philippine National Police chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said the minors were “rescued,” as the PNP beefed up its monitoring of online threats on school campuses.
STAR / File
MANILA, Philippines — Forty-nine minors have been rounded up in the past months for instigating cyber threats that disrupted school classes.
“These interventions show the value of timely information sharing and close coordination,” Nartatez said at a news briefing in Camp Crame.

There have been several school shootings perpetrated by disgruntled students, resulting in casualties and injuries among their schoolmates. The latest was a shooting in Banga, South Cotabato last Sept. 18 where three students, including the perpetrator, died.
By working with school authorities, local government units and other stakeholders, Nartatez said police units can assist in maintaining a safe environment for students, teachers and school personnel.
“Schools should be among the safest institutions or places for our children, which is why our police are present there,” he said.
In General Santos City, two students were apprehended for their threatening messages on a Facebook Messenger group chat on Saturday.
The suspects, known only as San and Henry, were apprehended after they exchanged messages in the online chat group accompanied by photographs of a firearm.
Nartatez said law enforcement operations are ongoing against online groomers who are manipulating youngsters to commit crimes.
“Our efforts are continuing. We have accounted for these personalities,” he said.

articles.title: Velasco couple a no-show at NBI probe
articles.summary: Former House speaker Lord Allan Velasco and his wife Rowena did not appear before the National Bureau of Investigation yesterday, sending their lawyers instead to respond to allegations made by…

MANILA, Philippines — Former House speaker Lord Allan Velasco and his wife Rowena did not appear before the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) yesterday, sending their lawyers instead to respond to allegations made by dismissed police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr.

articles.title: PCG: China disrupts law enforcement vs dynamite fishing
articles.summary: Chinese coast guard ships disrupted a Philippine law enforcement operation against suspected dynamite fishing near Pag-asa Island on Sunday, the Philippine Coast Guard reported.

blocks.text: October 6, 2026 | 12:00am

Rear Adm. Jay Tarriela, PCG spokesman for West Philippine Sea (WPS) issues, yesterday said personnel of the Joint Task Unit Pag-Asa reported sighting alleged blast fishing by a foreign vessel near Sandy Cays 2 and 3, about three nautical miles west of Pag-asa.
Screenshot from PCG

MANILA, Philippines — Chinese coast guard ships disrupted a Philippine law enforcement operation against suspected dynamite fishing near Pag-asa Island on Sunday, the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) reported.

Tarriela said the task force deployed boats in response, but China Coast Guard (CCG) ships with bow numbers 5102 and 21581 moved in their path, apparently as part of blocking maneuver at around 9:50 a.m.
“They sounded their horns and radio-challenged the Philippine team inside Philippine territorial waters,” he said.
Tarriela said the suspected blast fishing boats had already returned to their mother ship when the PCG came close at about 500 meters east-southeast of Sandy Cay 2.
“The team ordered the vessel to stop and radioed it several times. The vessel ignored these orders and sailed southwest toward Zamora Reef,” he said.
The PCG noted that CCG 21581 shadowed and blocked the Philippine boats as they followed the vessel, coming within about 10 yards of the PCG’s high-speed response boat.
“At 10:13 a.m., a People’s Liberation Army Navy helicopter (tail number 09) circled over the team four times,” he said.
For safety reasons, the PCG stopped pursuing the Chinese vessel after it reached 1.2 nautical miles east-southeast of Sandy Cay 5.
Tarriela said the law enforcement operation was carried out to stop destructive fishing practices and was not directed at any country.
“By obstructing Philippine authorities, the CCG did not protect the marine environment. It made it easier for a suspected violator to escape,” Tarriela added.
The deployment of a PLA Navy helicopter to obstruct a civilian law enforcement operation was an “unnecessary act of intimidation.”

Meanwhile, the AFP also reported that two Chinese military aircraft made dangerous maneuvers around a Philippine C-208 turboprop aircraft while the latter was on a routine maritime patrol over the WPS, particularly in the vicinity of Panatab Shoal last Saturday. — Mark Ernest Villeza, Emmanuel Tupas, Pia Lee-Brago

articles.title: Marcos vows better benefits, career growth for teachers
articles.summary: President Marcos vowed yesterday to further improve the benefits and career opportunities of Filipino teachers.

blocks.text: October 6, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos vowed yesterday to further improve the benefits and career opportunities of Filipino teachers.
Marcos said education remains a priority of his administration, with the sector receiving its biggest budget in the country’s history this year.

“We will not stop there. We will continue to find ways to further improve the support, benefits and opportunities for our teachers,” the President said in his speech at the “Teacher, Ikaw Naman” event at Smart Araneta Coliseum in Quezon City.

Marcos noted that 82,105 teachers and school heads had been promoted under the Expanded Career Progression System as of September, with another 135,000 targeted for promotion under the proposed 2027 national budget.
“Because supporting our teachers means investing in their growth, we have expanded opportunities for career advancement,” he said.

The government has also expanded benefits for educators, including doubling the annual non-taxable Teaching Allowance to P10,000, providing an annual medical subsidy of up to P7,000 and introducing five days of paid annual wellness leave.

Marcos likewise cited the P1,000 World Teachers’ Day Incentive Benefit, which public school teachers will receive starting Oct. 5, and said he had directed concerned agencies to ensure the orderly and faster processing of the 2024 Performance-Based Bonus.

“The success of our students, including our historic performance in PISA 2025, would not be possible without the sacrifice, dedication and skill of our teachers,” Education Secretary Sonny Angara said.
The celebration also recognized 16 exemplary teachers in Indigenous Peoples Education who have served remote indigenous communities for eight to 30 years.
The educators were recognized for partnering with community elders and culture bearers to develop learning resources tailored to ancestral domains.
Teachers’ march

To mark World Teachers’ Day, teachers marched to Mendiola to press the government to address their demands, accusing the Marcos administration of failing to deliver meaningful improvements to their working conditions.

Alliance of Concerned Teachers (ACT) representative Ruby Bernardo called on Marcos to move beyond recognizing teachers’ sacrifices and fulfill their long-standing demands for decent salaries, humane working conditions, adequately funded and nationalist education and an end to attacks on teachers’ rights and freedoms.

“More than any other celebration, World Teachers’ Day is a nationally coordinated protest by teachers to fight for the rights and well-being of our ranks, and for adequate funding and patriotic education. In the more than four years of the Marcos Jr. administration, there has been no significant change and the situation of teachers has become even more deplorable,” Bernardo said.
She also condemned the violence against teachers who staged a peaceful protest at the gates of Malacañang the previous day.

Bernardo warned that ACT would sustain collective action, including mass walkouts and strikes, if the administration continued to ignore and repress teachers and education workers, neglect basic social services and evade accountability.

“We will utilize our collective strength to advance the interests of our sector. We shall exhaust all available measures and exercise our constitutionally protected rights and freedoms to improve the conditions of millions of educators and the state of Philippine education – not only for our own benefit, but for the entire Filipino people whom we continue to serve,” she added.

Akbayan party-list Rep. Chel Diokno renewed his call for higher salaries and improved health care for public and private school educators, saying many continue to face financial difficulties despite their vital role in nation-building. — Delon Porcalla

articles.title: Marcos accepts resignation of Marina chief
articles.summary: President Marcos accepted yesterday the resignation of Maritime Industry Authority administrator Sonia Malaluan, who served the agency for almost 37 years.

blocks.text: October 6, 2026 | 12:00am
MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos accepted yesterday the resignation of Maritime Industry Authority (Marina) administrator Sonia Malaluan, who served the agency for almost 37 years.
“As far as I know – yes, it’s confirmed – it was accepted,” Palace press officer Claire Castro said.

In an official statement, Marina announced that Malaluan submitted her resignation letter to the Office of the President, stating her intention to retire effective Oct. 1 or until the President appoints a new administrator or designates an acting administrator.

“Pending the designation of a successor, Administrator Malaluan continues to perform her duties and responsibilities, in accordance with existing laws, rules and regulations,” Marina said in a statement.
The agency said it was the 60-year-old Malaluan’s “personal decision” to retire.
She was appointed by Marcos to head Marina on Dec.18, 2023, replacing Hernani Fabia.
Marina expressed its “appreciation to Administrator Malaluan for her service and leadership, and for her contributions to the continued development of the Philippine maritime industry.”

The maritime agency also assured stakeholders, partners and the maritime public that Marina will continue to operate, implement its programs and provide services without interruption during this change in leadership.
Marina said its officials and personnel would remain committed to fulfilling the agency’s mandate.
During her term as administrator, Malaluan followed a 10-point agenda, “Chartering a Clean Course: Safe Sailing Together” as her guide in targeting initiatives and priorities.

She pushed for digitalization of the agency’s frontline services such as blockchain enabled certification, enhanced the Integrated Seafarers’ Management Online, Maritime Energy Demand Information and Analysis Software, established a Shipping Online Ticketing System, developed the Public Assistance Information System, an Online Client Satisfactory Survey, and QR code-based feedback system to enhance maritime safety onboard inter-island passenger ships.

Malaluan rose from the ranks at Marina. Prior to being appointed as administrator, she served as deputy administrator for planning and was previously director of the agency’s different offices such as National Capital Region, manpower development, domestic shipping and management, financial and administrative services.
She was also a maritime attaché to London from December 2018 until December 2021.

articles.title: Chinese embassy on funneled funds: False narrative
articles.summary: Allegations that China funneled funds to a political faction in the Philippines are a “false narrative” and “malicious,” the Chinese embassy in Manila insisted yesterday.

blocks.text: October 6, 2026 | 12:00am
Former senator Antonio Trillanes IV presents financial transactions allegedly involving Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband Manases Carpio during a press conference October 4, 2026.
The STAR / Miguel De Guzman
MANILA, Philippines — Allegations that China funneled funds to a political faction in the Philippines are a “false narrative” and “malicious,” the Chinese embassy in Manila insisted yesterday.
Chinese embassy spokesman Ji Lingpeng did not name the Philippine faction and parties involved.

Last Friday, former senator Antonio Trillanes IV claimed that a foundation and a company associated with Vice President Sara Duterte and her husband Manases Carpio received more than P319 million in funds from the Chinese government and corporate sources.

Ji said the embassy has noted that certain Philippine politicians fabricated and spread a false narrative alleging that China had funneled funds to a political faction in the country, and that the embassy’s website has been maliciously linked to a redirect destination.

“We strongly condemn and firmly oppose such malicious rhetoric and actions. We urge the relevant individuals in the Philippines to stop political manipulation and not to drag Philippine domestic politics into China-Philippines relations,” Ji said.

“Attempts to achieve personal political gains by smearing and discrediting China and harming China’s interests and image are doomed to fail, and will ultimately undermine the interests of the Philippines and its people,” he added.
The embassy, Ji said, will take all necessary measures to safeguard its legitimate interests and dignity.
VP Sara ready
The Vice President is ready to face new charges after Defense Secretary Gilbert Teodoro urged Trillanes to turn over to authorities evidence relating to his latest allegations.

“She’s not running away from any case. She is facing all accusations. You have seen it. So, if there’s an investigation, then investigate because she’s confident that she’s on the right side,” her spokesman Paolo Panelo said.
Teodoro said Trillanes providing evidence would facilitate a thorough investigation on his latest allegations which, if substantiated, could raise serious implications on national security.

“His allegations are for parlor, not in court. Because in court, we follow rules of admissibility, you need to have personal knowledge, the evidence needs to be credible and clearly, he doesn’t have that. So, instead of appearing here (impeachment court) and being cross-examined by Vice President Sara’s defense team, he just held a press conference,” Panelo said.
Trillanes held a press conference on Friday after being dropped as prosecution witness and alleged that the money entered Cale88 Foods Corp., which he linked to the Vice President’s husband.
He said another P150 million went to the Tapang at Malasakit Foundation, where Duterte was identified as a member of the board of trustees.
Panelo denied that China is funding Duterte.

articles.title: Chiz calls for civility in impeach proceedings
articles.summary: Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero urged the public and concerned parties to let “civility” prevail over hotheads as Vice President Sara Duterte’s…

blocks.text: October 6, 2026 | 12:00am

MANILA, Philippines — Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero urged the public and concerned parties to let “civility” prevail over hotheads as Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial entered its 33rd day yesterday.

Escudero opened yesterday’s hearing with a quote from the late US Justice Sandra Day O’Connor: “The justice system cannot function effectively when the professionals charged with administering it cannot even be polite to one another.”
He did not indicate who he was referring to.

Escudero called for respect and civility even as the public and concerned parties are already getting impatient with the pace of the trial, while also vouching for the need to serve justice even if it means taking the long route.

“The chair understands that patience is wearing thin, tensions are running high and tempers are beginning to fray. But we must not lose sight of our common purpose. Our duty is not to prevail over one another, but to assist this court in the fair and orderly administration of justice,” Escudero said.
He reminded lawyers from both prosecution and defense of their code of conduct that “requires every lawyer to deal with fellow members of the Bar with courtesy, civility, fairness and candor.”

Addressing “non-lawyers” or interested parties in the trial, Escudero stressed the need to be civil to each other: “Disagreement may be vigorous and criticism unsparing, but no cause is strengthened by contempt. No institution is preserved by conduct, by conduct rather that strips another person of his or her dignity.

“Let the arguments be forceful, but never personal. Let the contest be exacting, but never degrading. And when these proceedings are concluded, let it be the law not anger, not pride, nor applause, be the final word,” he added. Escudero said the impeachment court would continue hearing the evidence so it could render fair judgment, and that it would “not be distracted nor detracted by the rantings or tantrums of anyone inside or outside this courtroom.”

“Because at the end of the day, it’s not about me, it’s not about you, it’s not about any one of us here. Rather, it is about the country, our people, accountability, justice and fairness,” Escudero added.
Bribery case out
The House prosecution reiterated yesterday its inclination to drop the bribery charges against Duterte, which constitutes Article III of the impeachment complaints.

“The panel will state its position formally before the Senate impeachment court. Our responsibility remains clear: to follow the evidence and bring a focused, well-supported case to its conclusion. That responsibility guides every decision we make,” lead prosecutor Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro said.

“We said from the very start that we would not drag out this impeachment trial, and we stand by that commitment. Filipinos have waited long enough for answers. Every hearing day must move the case forward,” she stressed.
Tongol reprimanded

Meanwhile, the Senate impeachment court reprimanded spokesman Reginald Tongol for last week’s comments regarding a possible Dec. 16 trial verdict, yet Escudero came to his defense, saying the verdict date was based on the impeachment timeline in the pre-trial order.
Sen. Raffy Tulfo called for the reprimand, noting that Escudero had previously warned both prosecution and defense counsels.

articles.title: Green party drops longstanding opposition to nuclear power
articles.summary:
Party in England and Wales ditches commitment to phase out nuclear in major shift in its energy policy

Green party members have voted to end the party’s opposition to nuclear power, dropping…

blocks.text: Green party members have voted to end the party’s opposition to nuclear power, dropping a commitment to phase out the technology in a major shift in its energy policy.

The motion, adopted at conference, removes a “blanket opposition to nuclear fission” and instead commits the Green party of England and Wales to assessing nuclear projects alongside other low-carbon technologies.

Its electricity generation policy still prioritises offshore wind, onshore wind and rooftop solar as the primary sources of electricity, but allows elected representatives to support new nuclear reactors on a case-by-case basis.

The Green MP Carla Denyer said the decision recognised there was a role for nuclear while the country moved towards an electricity system based primarily on renewables. “This evolution of our policy does not commit the party to backing new nuclear, but accepts this power source is here to stay for now, while we transition to electricity generation based primarily on renewable sources,” she said.

Denyer said keeping existing nuclear stations running could be a low-carbon option because a significant proportion of their carbon footprint came from construction. “So if I were energy secretary, my evidence-based approach would be to keep existing nuclear plants in operation, but to consider proposals for new nuclear power very carefully, bearing in mind the cost, speed and environmental impacts.”

Her comments strike a different tone from her assessment in 2023, when she described nuclear energy as “incredibly slow and incredibly expensive”. She said at the time: “Renewables is simply the way forward. Nuclear is not going to help us out in this climate emergency.”

Other senior Greens have previously criticised the technology. The party’s leader, Zack Polanski, has described it as outdated and compared investment in new nuclear reactors to “creating a fax machine”.

Last year, Adrian Ramsay, then a Green co-leader, criticised government support for Sizewell C. “The money being spent on this nuclear gamble would be far better spent on insulating and retrofitting millions of homes, bringing down energy bills and keeping people warmer and more comfortable,” he said.
The Green’s previous opposition to nuclear fission was rooted in its staunch opposition of nuclear weapons, one of the party’s founding principles.

Eugene McCarthy, a co-founder of Greens for Nuclear and a supporter of the motion, said the urgency of the climate crisis demanded a willingness to consider all available options. “We are at the throw-the-kitchen-sink-at-it phase of the climate crisis where you cannot be ruling anything out for things like Chernobyl happening in the 1980s,” he said.

The motion allows elected representatives to assess individual proposals on their merits, McCarthy said. “We will not say we support or don’t support any particular technology. This motion basically lets our elected members of parliament take it on a case-by-case basis and go: ‘This makes sense, we will extend the lifetime of Sizewell B,’ and on a different case say: ‘Actually the numbers don’t add up here.’”
after newsletter promotion

Asked about Polanski’s previous criticism of nuclear, McCarthy said the leader remained entitled to his views. “He’s still fully entitled to say that, and a lot of the nuclear technology that we are using is quite outdated, to be frank. What this means is that he can now take a nuanced position.”

Prof Andrew Stirling, who has advised government on nuclear power and energy policy, said the motion was “completely irrational”. “Why would a party that pioneered concerns about nuclear power that have been so broadly vindicated by history, choose now to shift its position?” he said.
“All authoritative sources agree that climate action is much faster, affordable and impactful with combined renewables and storage,” he added. “Why spend scarce resources on less effective actions?”
McCarthy said: “Renewables are cheaper and have much more capacity, and you can roll them out much quicker. [But] there are issues with baseload, which nuclear can help with.”

articles.title: France braces for national day of school protests as boy loses hand
articles.summary: Thousands expected to join marches of support on Tuesday across the country amid growing concerns over police response

blocks.text: France is bracing itself for a national day of protests and high-school blockades as a youth protest movement gathers pace amid a growing debate over the scale of the police response.

In one incident, a 15-year-old protesting against what demonstrators said were France’s dilapidated ⁠and understaffed ​schools ‌had his hand ‌blown off outside a high school in the northern town of Lens, the local prefect François-Xavier Lauch ‌said.

Lauch, the prefect of Pas-de-Calais, declined to comment on the exact circumstances, but said that between 150 and 200 protesters had been hurling a series of objects at police when riot officers intervened. It was uncertain if the incident had involved a police stun grenade or how the injury happened. Lauch said ​an investigation had ​been opened.

The family of a 16-year-old school pupil in Tours also filed a complaint about police violence after he lost sight in his right eye last week. The state prosecutor said the boy’s injuries were in line with the impact from a police rubber bullet. A police investigation is under way.
The French prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, had earlier attempted to calm the protests by accepting schoolchildren’s grievances as “legitimate” and saying the government must listen.

Lecornu ordered ministers to tackle the students’ five major demands. These include organising the replacement of absent teachers, in recognition that pupils in some areas miss months of teaching because of staff absences – even in key exam years. Lecornu also called for a review of France’s lengthy school days, which are among the longest in Europe.

The government will also look at repairs to dilapidated school buildings. Children on blockades across France have described water leaking into classrooms during class, cockroaches, collapsing ceilings and unbearable heat in summer. Lecornu said ministers must come up with proposals by the end of the month.

Sophie Binet, the head of the leftwing CGT trade union, said the government had been late in offering to tackle the schoolchildren’s demands. She said the number of absent teachers who were not replaced had doubled in 10 years and class sizes were at a record high.
“Amid such anger, a few measures just for show aren’t going to satisfy demands,” Binet said. She called for the government to instead stop all budget cuts as well as cuts to teachers’ positions.

Student unions have called for a national day of protest on Tuesday with more schools expected to be barricaded. Thousands of trade unionists, teachers, public sector workers and parents’ groups are expected to join marches of support in cities and towns across France.

Binet said trade unionists would march to ensure there was no violence on the edge of any protests on Tuesday, as she criticised heavy policing. “We’ve been appalled by what we have seen over the past 10 days and by the unprecedented crackdown that the government has organised against the protests by high school students,” she said.

University students continued to support the school protests on Monday, with up to 40 university buildings blockaded across France. Philippe Baptiste, the minister for higher education, told French radio he felt student and high school protests could intensify with the national protests due too take place on Tuesday.
after newsletter promotion
Between 400 and 500 high schools are expected to remain completely or partly closed on ⁠Monday out of a total of 3,700, the minister said.
A government spokesperson Maud Bregeon told CNews television on Monday: “Our priority is to restore order.”

The protests began in late September ‌at a high school ‌in a Paris suburb over teacher shortages. The government was taken by surprise as protests then spread nationwide, amid anger at social inequality and a lack of investment in the education system.
Since last Monday, about 5,000 people, mostly ‌teenagers, have been arrested across France and dozens injured.
Teachers have also been injured. Damage to property is estimated in the tens ​of millions of euros.

articles.title: Ukraine says Russian drones behind Turkish ship sinking
articles.summary: Romanian authorities did not say what caused the fire, but local media reported that the ship was carrying grain and was hit by a drone.

image.caption: Eleven crew members were rescued from the fireImage: Romanian Interior Ministry/Handout/REUTERS

blocks.text: Romanian authorities said on Monday that two people were killed and another one was wounded after a fire broke out in a commercial vessel on Romanian waters in the Black Sea.
The Turkish-owned civilian vessel subsequently sank. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the incident was caused by a Russian drone attack.

Romania's Interior Ministry said the Coast Guard was alerted at around 11 a.m. local time (14:00 UTC) and the afflicted vessel was in Romania's exclusive economic zone, some 30 nautical miles (55 kilometers) south of Sfantul Gheorghe in Tulcea County.
"Eleven crew members have been rescued. Two deceased individuals have also been located," the ministry said, adding that a helicopter had airlifted the injured.
Zelenskyy accuses Russia of 'horrific strike'
Authorities did not identify the cause of the fire, but Romanian media reported that the ship was carrying grain and was hit by a drone.

"A ‌horrific strike by two Russian drones on ‌a civilian vessel in neutral ‌waters carrying corn and owned by Türkiye. Azerbaijani and Indian citizens were on board," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote on X.
"As ⁠of now, unfortunately, we know that the ship's captain was ‌killed ... The fate of one other ⁠person is still being established," he added.
The Ukrainian government says it has repeatedly proposed taking steps to de-escalate the situation in the Black Sea, which is putting maritime trade at risk.
"But Russia consistently chooses terror and sinking civilian vessels instead of normal maritime navigation," Zelenskyy wrote on social media.
Rising threat to Black Sea maritime traffic

The Black Sea is a major commercial shipping route, which connects Ukraine's grain exports with the rest of the world. The waterway has faced heightened security concerns since Russia launched its full-scale war on Ukraine in 2022.
There has been an increase in war-related objects found in the Black Sea, mostly in Romanian, Bulgarian and Turkish waters, with analysts saying the trend is expected to continue.
The incident is the latest to take place on Romanian waters. In August, a Romanian F-16 fighter jet destroyed a marine drone near an offshore gas project in the Black Sea.
Two months before, a Ukrainian maritime drone exploded in Romania's Black Sea port of Constanta, with Ukraine saying the drone had been knocked off course by Russian electronic interference.

articles.title: 2027 budget projects thoroughly vetted, says House appropriations head
articles.summary: House Committee on Appropriations chairperson Mikaela Suansing on Monday said projects in the proposed 2027 national budget had undergone several layers of review, amid concerns raised by Senate…

blocks.text: Published October 5, 2026 11:34pm

House Committee on Appropriations chairperson Mikaela Suansing on Monday said projects in the proposed 2027 national budget had undergone several layers of review, amid concerns raised by Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian over alleged “red-flag” items.

In an interview, Suansing said the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) requires five documents for projects to be included in the 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP): a certificate of implementability and feasibility, actual program of works, Budget Preparation Form 202, approval from the regional or municipal development council, and geotagging.
The DPWH budget proposal is then reviewed by the Department of Budget and Management (DBM).
“We rely on DPWH and DBM’s word that these projects went through the proper vetting before they were even included in the NEP,” Suansing said.
She said the House Committee on Appropriations conducts another layer of review before projects are included in the House General Appropriations Bill.
“And then on the part of the House, there’s an additional layer of vetting for items that will be included in the House General Appropriations Bill,” Suansing said.
She added that for flood-control and drainage projects, Project NOAH and other members of the scientific community also help conduct additional validation.
Gatchalian had also flagged 189 items in the DPWH proposed budget as duplicates.
Suansing, however, said some of these may refer to different phases of the same project.
“It showed as a duplicate but actually, it is not. It’s a Phase 1 and Phase 2 of, example, a bypass road,” she explained.
Still, Suansing assured that the House would ensure that there are no actual duplications in the proposed budget.
“Most definitely, duplication in the sense na same station number, same coordinates, that one we’re looking through na wala dapat duplicate,” she said. —LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Sainsbury’s and Morrisons ‘held talks this year’ on multibillion-pound merger
articles.summary:
Deal would have created a supermarket with a market share of 23.6%, still well behind Tesco’s 27.8%

Sainsbury’s held merger talks with rival Morrisons this year to discuss a…

blocks.text: Sainsbury’s held merger talks with rival Morrisons this year to discuss a multibillion-pound deal that would have been the biggest shake-up for UK supermarkets in decades, according to reports.
The two companies held exploratory negotiations, according to the Financial Times and Sky. It is believed they are no longer in live discussions.
Morrisons, which was once one of the big four UK grocers alongside Sainsbury’s, Tesco and Asda, was bought by the US private equity firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice in 2021.
The deal loaded it with more than £7bn in debt on its balance sheet, and it has since struggled to grow as fast as its rivals. The German discounter Lidl overtook it in market share this year.

A merger between Sainsbury’s and Morrisons would have created a business with a 23.6% market share, putting it still some way behind Britain’s biggest retailer, Tesco, which has 27.8% of the market, according to analysts at Worldpanel by Numerator.

The last attempt to merge two of the big four supermarkets came in 2019, when Asda and Sainsbury’s almost joined forces. That £7bn deal was blocked by the Competition and Markets Authority on the basis that it would result in a loss of competition and higher prices for customers.
The CMA would have almost certainly reviewed any merger between Sainsbury’s and Morrisons, and could have required the former to sell some of its stores to gain approval for any deal.
Reducing competition in the grocery sector could also be politically sensitive, given that millions of households have grappled with persistent food inflation in recent years.

Clayton Dubilier & Rice, however, is open to a tie-up between Morrisons and another major supermarket, according to Sky. It reported that Asda, which is majority owned by the private equity firm TDR Capital, could also be drawn into deal talks.
Shares in Sainsbury’s, which is listed on the London Stock Exchange, were flat on Monday afternoon. The stock has fallen by 3% so far this year, compared with a 6% rise for its FTSE 100 rival Tesco.
Sainsbury’s, which employs about 140,000 people, is the second biggest grocer in the UK by market share at 15.2%.
after newsletter promotion
It agreed to sell Argos for £120m in the summer to allow it to concentrate on its core food business, a decade after buying the retail chain for more than £1bn.
News of supermarket takeover talks came as Lidl GB reported a 10% jump in its annual revenue to more than £13bn on Monday.

The company said pre-tax profits at its British arm rose by 30% to £245.5m in the year that ended in February as shoppers sought out cheaper fresh meat, fruit and vegetables, as well as its Deluxe upmarket food range.
Sainsbury’s and Morrisons declined to comment.

articles.title: Yemen air campaign against Houthis under way, says Saudi-led coalition
articles.summary:
Operation supported by 100 fighter jets said to have secured ‘air protection’ of Bab al-Mandab strait and destroyed hundreds of targets

Leaders of a Saudi-led coalition in Yemen claimed a…

blocks.text: Leaders of a Saudi-led coalition in Yemen claimed a broad air campaign involving 100 jet aircraft was under way on Monday against the Iran-backed Houthi rebels along the Red Sea coastline and farther north in the capital, Sana’a.

The Saudi coalition spokesperson, Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki, said the 100 fighter jets participating in Operation Dawn of Yemen were providing support to forces of Yemen’s internationally recognised government.

He said the coalition had secured “air protection” of the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait and destroyed hundreds of Houthi targets. He claimed hundreds of Houthis fighters had been beseiged in the Dhubab district, including the airport, close to the Bab al-Mandab strait, with some Houthi fighters fleeing across the Red Sea in boats.

blocks.caption: A man inspects the damage at a factory in Sana’a which was hit by an airstrike on Sunday. Photograph: Reuters

blocks.text: Southern Yemen forces known as the Giants Brigades, who are allied with the government, earlier on Monday launched a ground offensive against the rebels on the eastern flank of the coastal areas that the Houthis seized in their latest advances. The government forces also claim to have cut the road between Mocha and Dhubab, and that Houthi forces were deserting the recently captured city of Mocha as residents stayed behind closed doors.
Previous Saudi-led statements about territorial gains in recent weeks have often proved partial, but footage appeared to back up the Saudi claims of Houthis retreating by the seashore.

The president of the Saudi-backed government, Rashad al-Alimi, had promised a new offensive on Sunday, saying patience with the Houthis had run out. “Today we are embarking on a decisive phase in the history of our nation,” he said.

blocks.caption: Smoke rises from the site of an airstrike in Sana’a on Sunday. Photograph: Reuters

blocks.text: Airstrikes were also reported on Monday in Sana’a and the Houthi stronghold of Saada in the north of Yemen. Command and control centres, camps and weapons depots were targeted.
The Houthis, who captured Sana’a in 2014, have in recent weeks made lightning advances down the west coast of Yemen, reaching the Bab al-Mandab and seizing strategic islands on the strait.

On Monday Houthi sources denied reports of a retreat, and pointed to the explosions at a Saudi Aramco plant in Riyadh as a sign of the damage the group could still inflict on exposed Saudi oil installations, and by extension the world economy.

blocks.caption: Flames burn on Saturday at an oil facility south of Riyadh belonging to Saudi’s Aramco. Photograph: AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: It appears a political agreement reached between the two main external Arab actors in Yemen – Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates – permitted the UAE-backed Southern Giants to coordinate with the Saudi air force in the attack towards the coast.

It is being stressed by the Giants Brigades that no other ground forces supporting the Saudi-backed government are involved in the offensive. The Brigades, who are linked with the Southern Transitional Council, a political group outlawed in Yemen for trying to set up a secessionist state, are certain to have sought political commitments about the future status of Yemen in order to have thrown their military weight behind it.

It is not clear how the Saudis propose to address the age-old southern question. Concessions to the STC about the future governance of the south are certain to have been demanded, even if the UAE itself does not return to Yemen.

But the cooperation between the Saudi air force and the Giants Brigades is a remarkable turnaround, since only in January the Saudi air force was bombing UAE shipments of arms arriving in Southern Yemen for STC-backed forces.

The Saudi bombing triggered the UAE pullout from Yemen in January, the sudden dissolution of the STC, and the exile of its leader, Aidarous al-Zubaidi. At the weekend his supporters vowed to hold demonstrations later this month in support of the return to a separate southern state.
Houthi government officials claimed British fighter jets were supporting the Saudi air force with refuelling, something the UK Ministry of Defence has already announced.

The fighting was under way as senior ministers from Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia met in Riyadh to discuss the support Saudi Arabia might need to protect itself from the Houthis. They have formed a joint defence pact but it is not known how it will operate.

articles.title: US closely monitoring case of lab worker who ‘possibly’ died of plague in Siberia, says Rubio
articles.summary:
Quarantine measures in place in several hospitals in eastern Russia amid uncertainty over death of Darya Shipilova

The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, has said the US is closely…

blocks.text: The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, has said the US is closely monitoring the case of a Russian laboratory worker who died last week after a reported accident at a plague research institute in Siberia.

“We’re watching and monitoring it closely,” Rubio said on Monday before leaving for a trip to Europe. He added: “I ⁠don’t think it’s cause for alarm, but it is cause for focus and a cause just to keep an ⁠eye on it.”

Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old employee at the anti-plague institute in the city of Irkutsk, fell ill at work. She died two days later on the night of 2 October at a regional hospital in the nearby town of Shelekhov.

It remains unclear how she became unwell. Unconfirmed reports circulating in Russian media have suggested Shipilova may have been infected after a mishap at the laboratory. Officials have not publicly confirmed that account.

Local media have reported that the institute has subsequently been locked down, with staff forced to sleep on the floor and on chairs. “They’ve been isolating everybody since Friday – more than 60 people,” one relative, Roman, told the news portal Siberia.Realities.

He said family members were allowed to drop off food parcels at a checkpoint, while tests were carried out inside the isolated building. Similar quarantine restrictions have been placed on several other hospitals in and around the city.
Rubio, citing what ‌Russians have released about the death, said it seemed there was a worker in the lab who was ​infected and there was concern the disease may have spread internally.
“There’s very limited travel between the US and Russia, obviously,” he said. “But like anything else, something like that gets out, it just quickly spreads.“

Senior Russian officials have added to public disquiet by sending conflicting messages. Alexey Tsydenov, the head of the Buryatia region, which neighbours Irkutsk, initially wrote that Shipilova had died of plague, before editing his post to say she had “possibly” died of the disease.

Rospotrebnadzor, Russia’s health watchdog, said Shipilova died from “pneumonia of unknown aetiology”. It insisted that tests found no micro-organisms linked to her professional work and described the “sanitary and epidemiological” situation in the area as stable.

Authorities in the nearby city of Baikalsk briefly urged residents to avoid travelling to Shelekhov and surrounding settlements after what they said was unofficial information about a possible plague infection. They later deleted the post from social media.

“There are no obvious changes to daily life on the streets, but people are worried and anxious. Locals are angry that they are not being told anything,” said Elena Trifonova, a journalist with People of Baikal, an exiled Russian media outlet specialising on Siberia.

Despite the lack of a confirmed diagnosis, a series of precautionary measures appear to have been introduced across the region. The US-funded Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reported on Monday that several hospitals in Irkutsk had been placed under quarantine.
The outlet confirmed that staff from Shipilova’s workplace, the Irkutsk Anti-plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East, had been kept inside the institute since 2 October.

Patients at Irkutsk city clinical hospital No 1 and the Ivano-Matreninskaya children’s hospital said relatives were not being allowed to visit and people inside were not permitted to leave. There were similar quarantine measures at hospitals No 3 and No 10 and at least one maternity hospital.

Elsewhere, a mask requirement was introduced at the Irkutsk aluminium smelter in Shelekhov. The plant’s director, Artyom Fominykh, called it a preventive measure, saying: “Better safe than sorry.” Over the weekend several public events in Irkutsk were cancelled.

Shipolova’s death has also prompted intervention from senior federal health officials. Anna Popova, the head of Rospotrebnadzor and the country’s chief sanitary doctor, travelled to Irkutsk last Friday.
She attended an emergency meeting of the regional sanitary and anti-epidemic commission convened over what officials called a suspected case of a “particularly dangerous infection”.

Igor Kobzev, the governor of the Irkutsk region, urged residents to remain calm after meeting Popova to coordinate the response. “All identified contacts have been placed under medical observation. As of today, none is showing signs of illness and laboratory tests have returned negative results,” he wrote on Telegram.
Kobzev made no reference to reports that a laboratory worker had died.

US politicians have raised concerns about the incident, which follows longstanding and unfounded allegations by the Kremlin that Ukraine has secretly carried out biological weapons research, with the support of Washington.

A Republican representative, Don Bacon, a senior member of the House armed services committee, wrote on social media: “I remember hearing from anti-Ukraine voices about their so-called bio labs. It was Russian disinformation ops at their best. But in reality it is Russia with the bio labs.”
Plague remains endemic in parts of Siberia and the Russian far east, where the bacterium persists naturally among wild rodents and their fleas.

But human cases in Russia are rare. Before the suspected Irkutsk case, the country’s last recorded human infection was in 2016, when a 10-year-old boy in Siberia’s Altai Republic contracted plague after helping butcher a marmot.

“This case here seems like a rare lab accident and is unlikely to go much further,” Prof Ian Jones, professor of virology, University of Reading, said. “Although it is true that pneumonic plague is directly transmissible, the contacts of the primary case are known and can be treated if they show any sign of infection.”

He added: “Plague carries a huge history and is still present in many parts of the world including Russia, but the living conditions associated with previously spread plague are no longer generally true, antibiotics are available and its potential is therefore limited.”

articles.title: Supporters of Imran Khan start march on locked-down Islamabad
articles.summary: Pakistani authorities insist marchers calling for former PM to be released from jail will not reach the capital

blocks.text: Imran Khan’s supporters have begun a march to Islamabad to demand his release from jail after efforts by the government to halt the protest failed.
The march began in the former prime minister’s stronghold province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in north-west Pakistan on Sunday, according to leaders of his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party.

Concerns have grown over the health of the 74-year-old former Pakistan cricket captain who has been in prison since 2023. Party colleagues and family claim he is being held in solitary and has been denied visits by his doctor or relatives despite having a serious eye condition and high blood pressure.

The government had gone to extreme lengths to try to stop PTI holding the long march, including shutting down Islamabad and barricading the capital’s entrances with shipping containers and sandbags. Khan’s three sisters were among those detained last week on grounds of national security.
Two rounds of negotiations between the government and PTI leaders took place over the weekend but broke down when Khan’s allies insisted that he be part of political talks.

blocks.caption: Security officials at a checkpoint in Peshawar, the first major stop on the march by Imran Khan’s supporters. Photograph: Arshad Arbab/EPA

blocks.text: Attaullah Tarar, the information minister, accused the PTI of “double standards and hypocrisy”.

Thousands of supporters had joined the protest by Monday afternoon and the crowds are expected to grow on the way to Peshawar, the main city in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which the marchers should reach by Wednesday.
The march is being led by the province’s chief minister, Sohail Afridi, who described those taking part as “Imran Khan’s soldiers”.
“I call upon you all to come out, the youngsters to come out for the sake ​of your leader who is sitting in jail,” he said.

Khan was prime minister from 2018 to 2022, when he was toppled by a parliamentary vote of no confidence. Since then, he and the PTI have faced mounting government pressure, which culminated in his arrest in 2023. The harassment and detention of other PTI leaders continues.

Khan is widely considered the country’s most popular politician, while the ruling coalition government, which is backed by the military, is facing discontent over an economic crisis and a surge in terrorism.
Ministers say the march is illegal and all measures will be taken to ensure it does not break through the capital’s boundaries.

Tens of thousands of police and paramilitary personnel were deployed to Islamabad and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa last week, raising fears that Khan’s supporters will be met with state violence. Government politicians falsely claimed that the PTI was allowing militants from the Pakistan Taliban to take part in the march.
Opposition leaders fear the prime minister will impose emergency rule on Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to stop the march.

articles.title: Relatives of Epstein victim appear in attack ad targeting Republican congressman
articles.summary:
Family of Virginia Giuffre criticizes Colorado’s Jeff Crank for voting to block a vote to release the Epstein files

Two relatives of Virginia Giuffre, one of the most prominent Jeffrey…

blocks.text: Two relatives of Virginia Giuffre, one of the most prominent Jeffrey Epstein victims who died last year, appeared in a political attack ad targeting Colorado Republican congressman Jeff Crank, accusing him of refusing to meet with them.
Sky Roberts, Giuffre’s brother, and his wife, Amanda Roberts, expressed disappointment that Crank had voted to block a vote to release the federal investigative files relating to Epstein.

The couple claimed that Crank, who later supported the Epstein Files Transparency Act which authorized the release of a tranche of documents in a near-unanimous vote, refused to meet with them in Washington.

“My sister Virginia was one of Jeffrey Epstein’s victims. She spent her life trying to expose the truth. After she died, we promised to carry on her fight,” Sky Roberts said in the ad backing Crank’s opponent, Democrat Jessica Killin.

“But our own congressman Jeff Crank refused to meet with us,” Amanda Roberts continued. “Then, when he had the chance to expose the truth and release the Epstein files, he repeatedly voted to cover them up.”

The couple have become increasingly politically active. Over the summer they urged senators on the Senate judiciary committee to block the confirmation of attorney general Todd Blanche. They also criticized a decision by the Department of Justice to restrict the release of unredacted files to Epstein investigators in New Mexico.
They also appeared at Donald Trump’s State of the Union address in February as guests of Maryland congressman Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House judiciary committee.
Epstein has become a major issue for Donald Trump amid public unhappiness over the presidential administration’s handling of the issue.

While Democrats are largely focusing on economic issues ahead of the midterm elections, the Epstein issue has cropped up in some races, though the Colorado ad is the first to feature family members of an Epstein victim.

An ad funded by a Democratic group in Maine accused Republican senator Susan Collins of voting “with Trump to cover up the Epstein files” and “protecting child predators” and another political ad in Iowa accused Republican congresswoman Ashley Hinson of accepting donations from people named in the files. They have not been accused of wrongdoing.

“I would like to tell Ashley Hinson that I don’t trust you. If you can’t stand up for girls and women in Iowa and the rest of this country, why should I ever vote for you?” a woman says in the voiceover of the ad.

The New York Times has identified 35 congressional races with ads that mention Epstein, though most appear to reference the financier in the context of the “Epstein class”, a phrase used to assemble opposition to an idea of unaccountable or excessive wealth in the US.
The outlet noted that attack ads deploying “Epstein” lack reference to the reversals of the lawmakers positions on the document release.
Sky and Amanda Roberts told the New York Times that they met with Crank’s district director after joining protests against his re-election in the district.

“At the end of the day, the bare minimum of this job in this role is to hear your constituents,” Sky Roberts said, relaying his conversation with Crank’s aide. “How can you stay with your constituents and vote according to their needs if you have no idea what their needs are?”
Simon Andriesz, a whistleblower and former Wall Street banker who alerted Congress to commerce secretary Howard Lutnick’s ties to Epstein, died by suicide last week.

articles.title: Zelensky condemns 'horrific' Russian strike on boat carrying corn in Black Sea
articles.summary: The vessel's captain was killed and 11 crew members were rescued after the attack on the Turkish-owned ship, Ukraine's leader says.

blocks.text: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has condemned a "horrific" Russian attack on a vessel carrying corn in the Black Sea.
The ship's captain was killed in the strike involving two drones, Zelensky said, and another sailor was unaccounted for. Eleven crew members - nationals of Azerbaijan and India - have been rescued.
Romania said it had mounted a rescue mission after "a fire on the ship Royad Mammadov" outside the country's territorial waters. It said two people had died.

Russia has not commented, but its defence ministry earlier said it had struck two cargo vessels. Russia has been pounding Ukrainian infrastructure in what it says is retaliation for Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries and ships in the Black Sea.
Monday's attack by Russia targeted "a civilian vessel in neutral waters carrying corn and owned by Turkey", Volodymyr Zelensky said.
He did not give the location of the ship, but Romania's interior ministry said it had sunk about 30 nautical miles south of its port of Sfantu Gheorghe.

"At around 11:00 (09:00 GMT), Coast Guard border police officers were informed that a fire had broken out on board a commercial vessel located within Romania's exclusive economic zone," the ministry said in a statement.
"Eleven crew members have been rescued. Two deceased persons have also been identified," it added.
Ukraine's president said he had "repeatedly proposed concrete steps to de-escalate the situation and ensure security in the Black Sea" - and other countries had made "relevant proposals" too.
"But Russia consistently chooses terror and sinking civilian vessels instead of normal maritime navigation," Zelensky said.
"Pressure is needed to restore global food security," he added. "And everyone who is genuinely interested in this must help."

On Sunday, Russia's defence ministry said it would intensify its strikes across Ukraine in response to comments made by Zelensky earlier last week, in which he said Kyiv would ramp up its attacks on Russian oil refineries.
Ukraine maintains it began attacking Russian oil infrastructure because it helped the Kremlin finance the war which began with Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.
President Vladimir Putin admitted last week Kyiv had "got some results" from its refinery attacks and Russia had lost about 1% of its GDP.
The Russian leader has also intensified his rhetoric against Western allies of Ukraine - repeating a threat of even using nuclear weapons.
Western allies have faced a surge in so-called hybrid warfare incidents blamed on Russia, particularly in Poland and the Baltics in recent months.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said last Thursday that his country was preparing for further hybrid attacks, "including serious ones", after a drone armed with explosives was found in August on the tarmac at Leipzig airport close to Ukrainian cargo planes.

The head of Germany's foreign intelligence Martin Jaeger said on Monday that "Germany is in danger of becoming embroiled in a violent conflict with Russia", which was "waging a shadow war" with the threat of attacks against targets in Germany remaining "real and imminent".

“There are considerations we are addressing, and this is what we meant when we said that while there are discussions…serious inclinations towards withdrawing Article 3, until we are yet to tell it to the impeachment court, it does not become official,” she added.

One of the allegations under the four Articles of impeachment is that the Vice President should be impeached for giving monetary gifts or payments to DepEd officials to induce the violation and circumvention of procurement and other related laws.
During the same press conference, Luistro assured the public that their evidence against the Vice President is strong, including in the bribery allegation.

“We are confident because our evidence is complete and strong for all four Articles concerning grave threats, confidential fund [misuse], unexplained wealth, and even bribery. If ever there are discussions about the possibility of withdrawing bribery, that is only in consideration of our commitment not to drag this trial too much,” Luistro said.
“We wanted to expedite this proceeding for the best interest of the Filipino people,” she added.

articles.summary: The Flydubai pilot from Oman suspected of trying to crash a plane in Israel spent time in Oceania as a young man. Police in both Australia and New Zealand said they would investigate his links to the…

image.caption: The copilot is suspected of hijacking the Israel-bound flight with a view to crashing it intentionally, attacking his pilot with the emergency ax in the cockpit in the process (FILE: September 30, 2026)Image: Gil Cohen-Magen/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Security agencies in Australia and New Zealand on Monday said they were investigating the time that the co-pilot of Flydubai flight FZ1073 spent in the countries in his youth

The Omani national is in custody in the United Arab Emirates. He is suspected of attacking his pilot Smit Machchhar with the emergency ax in the cockpit, and attempting to hijack the plane and crash it intentionally in Israel.

The pilot and passengers combined to thwart his attempts and restrain him. After a near-vertical dive lasting around 30 seconds during the fight for control, the plane made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.
What did Australian and New Zealand authorities say about the case?

The Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT) said on Monday that the man had enrolled at the Melbourne university in the state of Victoria, but said that he did not successfully complete an engineering qualification.

A spokesman for the Australian Federal Police said that the Victorian Counter Terrorism Team — comprising federal poice, Victorian state police, and the ASIO intelligence agency — was "investigating the man's links to Australia."
Based on Australian media reports, the man arrived on an Australian student visa in 2014, enrolled in 2015, left in 2017, and had his visa canceled in 2019.
Flydubai passengers recount terror after hijacking attempt
Similarly, police in New Zealand said on Monday that the suspect spent time there, without specifying exactly where or when.

"We are looking into the time he spent here, alongside other agencies where appropriate," New Zealand Police assistant commissioner Micahel Johnson told the RNZ news outlet, issuing similar comments elsewhere. "We are unable to comment further at this time."
Flight FZ1073's pilot, Indian national Machchhar, also spent some of his formative years in New Zealand. He completed his early flight training some 18 years ago with the Mainland Air carrier.

"I was really pleased to read how he handled the situation," the airline's chief executive Philip Kean told RNZ. "He got through and he got the door open so the other people could save the airplane, because if he hadn't done that, it would have been a disaster."

articles.title: In both France and Spain, ruling parties must prove they can give young protesters hope
articles.summary: Demonstrations over housing rights and crumbling schools are a sign the younger generation is withdrawing political consent

blocks.text: In Spain, tens of thousands of people in 50 cities have taken to the streets amid mounting fury over the country’s housing crisis, their feelings made plain on a banner at the burgeoning protest camp in Madrid’s Puerta del Sol plaza: “You can speculate on watches, jewels, crypto-bros and Ferraris. But not on our fucking homes.”

In France, as high school pupils clash with police in often violent protests over long hours, missing teachers, crumbling classrooms and an opaque university admissions system, the angry slogans include: “More hours in class than for sleep”, “Fund study, not repression” and “I’d like to be worrying about my maths exam, not my future.”

blocks.caption: Demonstrators clash with police officers during a student protest in Nancy, France. Photograph: Muhammed Said Tako/Anadolu/Getty Images

blocks.text: They may stem from different specific grievances, but the two waves of mainly youth-led protest exemplify a growing problem for western European governments: a generation of young people feeling increasingly denied the basic socioeconomic security that, by and large, their parents enjoyed.

The trigger in Spain, where rents have risen by 80% in a decade, was – perhaps ironically – the high-profile eviction of an 87-year-old woman in Madrid after an investment fund hiked her rent by 230%. For those spending over half their income on housing (the monthly rental on a one-bedroom flat can cost an entire median salary), enough was enough.

Rocketing rents, rampant property speculation, the boom in short-term tourist rentals and stagnant wages have combined to make an independent adult life increasingly unachievable for many young workers – and the state is seen not as a neutral mediator, but an active enabler of property speculation.

In France, the protests began in the northern Paris suburbs but quickly spread nationwide, fuelled by young people’s anger at an underfunded education system that, the data shows, entrenches social inequality.

Pupils routinely miss months of teaching owing to unfilled staff absences. Timetables run from 8am to 6pm – among the longest in Europe – in buildings with leaking roofs, cockroaches and collapsing ceilings. In Paris last week, students on high school barricades saw budget cuts as a straightforward assault on their future. In their eyes, a system meant to promote social mobility now prevents it.

Lacking parliamentary majorities and facing varying degrees of budgetary constraint, however, neither government has much room for manoeuvre. Spain’s socialist prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, on Monday called a snap general election after rightwing parties voted down his emergency housing legislation.

blocks.caption: Tents at a housing protest encampment at the Puerta del Sol in Madrid. Photograph: Borja Sanchez-Trillo/EPA

blocks.text: In France, as student protests – and more than 5,000 arrests – forced the closure of up to 500 secondary schools on Monday, the centrist prime minister, Sébastien Lecornu, has urged local authorities to prioritise filling long-term teacher absences and called urgent meetings to discuss repairing dilapidated school buildings

Taken together, the two crises highlight some core problems facing mainstream governments. First, young people in particular have come to see incremental measures – targeted tax credits, minor administrative reforms – as sticking plasters on altogether deeper socioeconomic wounds.

Second, facing mounting street pressure and opposition parties eager to exploit it, ruling coalitions – especially those that lack majorities – will struggle. And in France, heavy-handed policing risks alienating young voters from the mainstream even further.
after newsletter promotion

Meanwhile, radicalised opposition parties are actively weaponising the discontent. On the radical left, France’s Jean-Luc Mélenchon – backed by 47% of voters under 35– has sided openly with the street, while in Spain, leftwing parties Podemos and Sumar have blamed the housing crisis squarely on out-of-control financial capitalism.

At the same time, the populist far right is playing a law-and-order card, with Marine Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) in France seizing on footage of burning barricades to accuse centrist leaders of tolerating “unbridled violence” and Spain’s far-right Vox siding with the main conservative Partido Popular opposition to torpedo Sánchez’s emergency package, framing it as government overreach punishing landlords.

blocks.caption: Students of Lycée Sophie Germain demonstrate and blockade their school on 5 October. Photograph: Tom Nicholson/Getty Images

blocks.text: Squeezed from both sides, mainstream governments face a spiralling challenge. When an entire generation concludes that society’s existing frameworks guarantee them neither affordable homes nor functioning schools, political consent starts to evaporate and Europe’s establishment parties risk losing their legitimacy.

As Nando ‌de Anguulo, a 26-year-old protester in Madrid, put it: the protests prove that as things stand, “it ‌is us, the people, who have to adapt to the political parties – and not the politicians who have to adapt to what the people want. It can’t go on like that.”

articles.title: Yemeni government forces say they have 'secured' Bab al-Mandab Strait
articles.summary: Houthi-run media deny the government has made advances in the Dhubab area, which overlooks the strategic Red Sea waterway.

blocks.text: Yemeni pro-government forces backed by Saudi Arabia say they have "secured" the Bab al-Mandab Strait at the start of a major offensive against the Iran-backed Houthi movement.

A Yemeni military spokesman said Giants Brigades and National Shield forces were besieging Houthi fighters in the Red Sea coastal town of Dhubab, which overlooks the strategic waterway, after the forces took control of its airport and cut the road to the port city Mokha.
Houthi-run media denied that government forces had made advances in the Dhubab area.
The government said operations had also begun on several other fronts, including the capital Sanaa, which fell to the Houthis at the start of the civil war 12 years ago.
Meanwhile, a Saudi-led military coalition said its fighter jets had destroyed more than 300 "high-value" targets in strikes supporting the offensive.

On Sunday, the head of Yemen's internationally recognised Presidential Leadership Council announced the beginning of an offensive aimed at retaking all territory held by the Houthis, insisting that all opportunities for de-escalation had been exhausted.

Rashad al-Alimi called on all armed forces, security forces and military formations "to begin carrying out their assigned missions, in accordance with the approved plans, until the country is liberated from the grip of the Houthi terrorist militia".
It came after the Houthi fighters reportedly cut a mountain road near the south-western city of Taiz, effectively leaving government forces and residents there surrounded.

The Houthis also said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at oil sites belonging to Saudi Aramco in Riyadh and the Khurais area of Saudi Arabia in retaliation for dozens of Saudi strikes on their territory.

Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after a Saudi-led coalition of Arab states intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule.

A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
The Houthis said they were retaliating for a Saudi blockade of ports and airports in their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom.

Last month, the Houthis launched a surprise offensive along Yemen's south-western Red Sea coast and quickly ousted pro-government forces from areas overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait, including Dhubab, Mokha and Perim (Mayyun) Island.
They said they posed no threat to international shipping passing through the waterway but that they would continue to target vessels from Saudi Arabia.
At least 959 people have been killed and 5,000 injured in the fighting in Yemen since 6 August, according to the government's health ministry.
The UN says another 197,000 people have been displaced.
